doc.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Wings memorabilia on the studio wall
summary: He identifies his platinum Back to the Egg album and photos from his time in Wings, 1978-81, including the Rockestra session, Goodnight Tonight video, the Hammersmith Palais and Ken MacIntosh band, a Diablo 3 award and a Cavern Club photo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Isolation booths have taken on an added meaning, yeah. So people who watch this are going to want to know, over your right shoulder is a shiny record and over your left shoulder —
The shiny record, that’s a platinum album for Wings, “Back to the Egg.”

I was in Wings from ’78 to ’81. And the picture next to that is Paul McCartney with a concertina sitting on the balcony of a castle, a twelfth century castle on the south coast of England when we were recording. The one above that is Linda McCartney at a Hammond B3 organ, and you can’t really see clearly but on top of the organ there is a pack of Senior Service, Players Senior Service cigarettes, no filtertips, which is what Paul smoked at the time. There’s a cup of tea, a scotch and Coke, a bunch of boxes of Kodak recording film at which you could run a very high ISO so you didn’t have to use flash, because flash photography in a studio situation is kind of a no-no. It’s too distracting. And that was during the Rockestra session when we had not only Wings in Abbey Road Studio, but we also had the, it was like members of the Who, Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, it was crazy. It was a rock orchestra. This side, that’s me with Wings when we were filming a video of a hit song we had called “Goodnight Tonight.” And so the Hammersmith Palais, which is a venue in London with a revolving stage that I used to play at when I was just getting into studio work. I played with, there was a band, Ken MacIntosh, who was a band leader and had one of those kind of three saxes and two trumpets, trombone, rhythm section kind of playing hits of the day. And it was always good sight reading practice for me. And then let’s see up top is an award I got of my co-composing of the score of “Diablo 3” which was a videogame that I did composing on. And then below that is a picture that Mike McCartney, Paul’s brother took in I think 1961 of Paul, John and Gene Vincent at the Cavern Club in Liverpool. And then below that is just a bunch of acoustic guitars.
